clue.text: Crown princess owned those things in 'ackney

blocks.note: Di, the familiar name of Princess Diana
owned is 'had', said with the H dropped

explanation.surface: A cockney points out that a crown was the princess's own property.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a working-class East London borough, and 'in 'ackney' tells you to speak like a cockney, who drops H: had becomes 'AD and them becomes 'EM, the theme of the whole puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled headband or circlet worn by royalty, a kind of crown.

clue.text: One's not normally for putting 'eadless 'orseman of legend without an aitch

indicators.note: with no head means the word's first letter is dropped
going without the letter H means that letter is removed from what remains

blocks.note: Chiron was a centaur of Greek myth, half man and half horse

explanation.surface: A golfer is told which club not to use, next to a cockney tale of the Headless Horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Headless Horseman suggests Sleepy Hollow, but the legendary horse-man is the centaur Chiron: lose the head C and the H and IRON is left.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an iron is a club for approach shots from the fairway; a separate putter is used on the green.

clue.text: 'ard up. With support, finally overcomes disadvantages

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, back to front
finally points to the very end of a word, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: W is the usual abbreviation for with
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone hard up gets financial backing and at last beats their handicaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ard up' reads as broke, but it is HARD minus its H, written upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawbacks are snags or downsides, so the plural noun matches disadvantages as a synonym.

clue.text: Lay 'im out with third of punches for the most part

indicators.note: laid out means spread around anyhow, so these letters are rearranged
the third of a word is its third letter, the only one kept

explanation.surface: A boxer is urged to knock his opponent flat, mostly with punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay out' is boxing slang for knocking someone down, but here 'out' scrambles LAY and IM plus the N from punches.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly is an adverb meaning chiefly or mostly, the same sense as the phrase about most of something.

clue.text: Plant's 'ealing mixture with added calcium

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order
adding one thing to another puts the extra letters alongside

blocks.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy for healing is boosted with calcium.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a London borough, so 'ealing looks like a place, but it is healing in cockney; it is mixed with CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is a tall aromatic herb whose candied stems are used in cakes, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Small broadcasting companies 'ad first run in with governments

indicators.note: coming first means placed at the front of everything else
something put in another goes inside it

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Little radio stations got into trouble with the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a run-in with' sounds like a clash with officialdom; in fact AD goes first and R goes into MINI STATIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: An administration is the ruling body or executive of a country, so administrations are its ruling governments.

clue.text: In Britain I wager 'e'd get 'anged

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: A cockney bets that a man would be hanged in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself dropped-H: 'anged is hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is a gallows, so to be gibbeted is to be hanged or displayed on one after execution.

clue.text: Enjoyed long walk over 'ills 'n' dales initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only first letters are used

blocks.note: a walk over hills is a hike, said with the H dropped

explanation.surface: A rambler enjoyed a long tramp across hills and dales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' serves both long and dales, which take their first letters either side of 'IKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liked is the past tense of like, meaning took pleasure in, so it swaps for enjoyed.

clue.text: It's 'andy 'e's been found in ... in ... in a nunnery!

indicators.note: to be found in a place is to be inside it
placed in something means put within it

explanation.surface: A scandalised cry that a man has been discovered inside a nunnery, which is handy for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Andy is handy without its H. The dots let one 'in' serve as letters while the others act as signals, so the insertion happens twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient is handy: easy to reach or use, suited to one's needs.

clue.text: Support for King 'enry is following Yorkist leader invading most of capital

indicators.note: following means coming after, so these letters are placed behind
most of a word is all but its last letter
an invader enters territory, so these letters go inside the others
the leader is the one at the front, so just a first letter

blocks.note: Hal, the nickname of Prince Henry in Shakespeare, without the H

explanation.surface: A history lesson: backing for King Henry follows a Yorkist leader's invasion of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is Hal, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal, so the cockney 'enry drops that H. 'King' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalism is allegiance to monarchy, so it is backing for a king and his crown.

clue.text: Ridin' an 'arley? Put on one's 2-piece suit!

indicators.note: to put something on is to add it at the end

blocks.note: riding a Harley-Davidson is biking, with the G and H dropped
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A biker is told to change into a two-piece suit before riding a Harley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' looks like getting dressed, but it adds I to BIKIN', where both the G of riding and the H of Harley go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a woman's swimsuit in two separate parts, top and bottom.

clue.text: After renovation it 'ad clean bed and good food to eat

indicators.note: a renovation rebuilds and rearranges, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A refurbished boarding house now offers a clean bed and decent meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a B&B review; the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A balanced diet mixes the right proportions of nutrients, so it is wholesome eating.

clue.text: Make endless changes salient 'ere

indicators.note: something that changes takes a different form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep making changes to the main points here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless changes' suggests constant revision; 'endless' belongs to the definition and 'changes' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To eternalise something is to make it last for ever, without any end.

clue.text: For the ear is sexy, but not 'er

indicators.note: but not excludes something, so those letters are taken away

explanation.surface: Someone finds an ear sexy, though not the woman it belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ER from EROTIC to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective relating to the ear, as in otic drops.

clue.text: 'e's cleaner in second movie in particular

indicators.note: one thing in another goes inside it

blocks.note: Cif is a brand of household cleaning cream
S is the abbreviation for second
a pic is a film, short for picture

explanation.surface: A cameo: he plays the cleaner in the sequel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cif is a brand of kitchen and bathroom cleaning cream sold in Britain. The second 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific and particular are adjectival synonyms, both meaning relating to one definite thing.

clue.text: Demanding old Bob gets under 'is canvas for cover

indicators.note: getting under something means going beneath and inside it, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: under his canvas is in his tent, with the H dropped
a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A bossy man called Bob shelters beneath his tarpaulin.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a name, but a bob was the old British shilling, written s. Being under canvas means in a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: An insistent person keeps pressing a demand and will not take no, so is demanding.

clue.text: Ran em out 'n' got in 'n' settled in nicely

indicators.note: out means removed, so one letter leaves
getting in means entering, so another letter takes the vacant place

blocks.note: to run goods is to smuggle them
em is the name of the letter M
'n' as in fish 'n' chips, the letter N

explanation.surface: Smugglers ran contraband, slipped back in and made themselves comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: Ran, as in gun-running, is SMUGGLED; the M (em) goes out and N comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuggle is to nestle cosily, so snuggled describes settling comfortably into place.

clue.text: Captive's lying about 'is rank at first

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another
at first points to the start, so the opening letter alone

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war falsifies his rank when first questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests telling lies, but here it means lying down: PRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive is someone held against their will, the same as a prisoner.

clue.text: Misbe'ave, lacking character after function

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so this letter is placed at the end

explanation.surface: Someone behaves badly, showing no moral character after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking character' reads as spineless, but it is the letter the clue's own apostrophe stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinh is the hyperbolic sine, a mathematical function written alongside cosh and tanh.

clue.text: Makes mad cloakroom things to put 'oodies and 'arringtons on

definitions.text: cloakroom things to put 'oodies and 'arringtons on

blocks.clueFragment: cloakroom things to put 'oodies and 'arringtons on
blocks.note: second meaning: coat hangers, said with the H dropped

explanation.surface: Not having anywhere to hang your hoodie and jacket is maddening.
explanation.walkthrough: A Harrington is a short zipped British jacket and a hoodie a hooded top; the things you hang them on are hangers, which a cockney says without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a verb meaning enrages, while the second sense is the plural noun hangers pronounced cockney style.

clue.text: Flags 'n' signpost 'ave blown about

indicators.note: things blown about by wind land scattered in a new order

blocks.note: 'n' is N and 'ave is have without its H

explanation.surface: Bunting and a road sign have been knocked over by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Flags look like banners, which suits 'blown about', but they are flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag, or flagstone, is a flat slab used for paving, so flags are paving stones.

clue.text: Deduce no much-quoted poem's been written about 'er

indicators.note: written around something means wrapped about it

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for no

explanation.surface: A reader concludes that no famous poem has ever been written about her.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's If is regularly voted Britain's favourite poem; it is written around N, then 'ER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, so it means deduce.

clue.text: Fragrant oil 'eated at temperature above zero

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means placed earlier in the column

blocks.note: heated is hot, with the H dropped
T is the abbreviation for temperature
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Aromatic oil is warmed to just above freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At temperature above zero' reads as a reading on a thermometer, but it is T placed over O.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto, also attar, is an essential oil distilled from rose petals and used in perfume.

clue.text: Tour of Paris 'e's provided freely on odd occasions

indicators.note: odd occasions are the first, third and fifth times, so alternate letters

explanation.surface: A guide occasionally offers a free tour of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Tour is French for tower, so this tour is the famous landmark rather than a sightseeing trip.
explanation.definitionFit: La Tour Eiffel is the Parisian name of the Eiffel Tower, so the word completes that French name.

clue.text: 'ouse rented by Taiwanese on vacation wanting egg fu yung?

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: house is home, with the H dropped
a let property is rented out

explanation.surface: A holiday home rented by a Taiwanese visitor who fancies a Chinese takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: egg fu yung is one kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg foo young is a Chinese-American dish of beaten eggs fried with fillings, a type of omelette.

clue.text: Puts down university qualifications the second 'e 'ad succeeded

indicators.note: to succeed someone is to take over their position, so one piece replaces another

blocks.note: the second E of the qualifications

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at university degrees the moment he has passed his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The second 'e' looks like 'the moment he', but it is literally the second letter E of DEGREES, which AD replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to humiliate or belittle them, so degrades means belittles.

clue.text: Front of 'ouse filled 20 rows

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
something filled has another thing put inside it

blocks.note: the answer to 20 across; setts are granite paving blocks

explanation.surface: The first row of the stalls has filled twenty rows.
explanation.walkthrough: Front of house is theatre language; here it is the O of 'ouse inside SETTS, a word for the 20 across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a quarrel or fight, and a row in the British sense is a noisy argument.
